color.note: Semantic names only. Nothing in the app references a hex value or a primitive ramp; if a colour is needed that no token names, the token is missing. Light is authored first, dark is authored beside it — neither is a tint of the other.

tokens.name: surface-canvas
tokens.usage: The window ground behind every pane. Sidebar, gutters and the space between panes.

tokens.name: surface-base
tokens.usage: The reading surface of a pane: run tree, timeline, forms, tables. Default ground for ink-primary, ink-secondary and ink-tertiary.

tokens.name: surface-raised
tokens.usage: Things that float: command palette, popovers, menus, the gate card, dialogs. Pair with shadow-popover, never with a heavier border.

tokens.name: surface-sunken
tokens.usage: Wells that hold machine text: the agent output pane, YAML source view, artifact body, diff gutters.

tokens.name: surface-overlay
tokens.usage: Scrim behind a modal dialog or the command palette. Never carries text.

tokens.name: surface-hover
tokens.usage: Row and control hover. Layered over whatever ground is beneath, so it works on base, raised and sunken alike.

tokens.name: surface-active
tokens.usage: Pressed state for rows and controls, and the ground of an open disclosure header.

tokens.name: surface-selected
tokens.usage: The selected run tree row, selected timeline entry, selected grid cell. Keyboard selection uses this plus border-focus, never this alone.

tokens.name: border-hairline
tokens.usage: Purely decorative separation: row rules, pane splits, table lines. Structure in this system is drawn with hairlines instead of shadows. Exempt from the 3:1 floor because removing it never hides a control — anything that must be seen to be used takes border-default.

tokens.name: border-control
tokens.usage: The boundary that identifies an interactive control or a graph node: inputs, buttons, selects, checkboxes, workflow and dependency nodes. Holds 3:1 on surface-canvas, surface-base, surface-raised and surface-sunken in both themes.

tokens.name: border-strong
tokens.usage: Emphasis edge: hovered control, the frame of an expanded step, a graph node on the executed path. 5:1 or better on every pane ground in both themes.

tokens.name: border-focus
tokens.usage: The 2px focus ring, drawn outside the control with a 1px offset. At least 3:1 on canvas, base, raised, sunken and every status tint in both themes.

tokens.name: ink-primary
tokens.usage: Body copy, row labels, headings, values. On surface-canvas, surface-base, surface-raised, surface-sunken and every status tint.

tokens.name: ink-secondary
tokens.usage: Supporting text that still must be read: timestamps, durations, field help, secondary columns. On surface-base and surface-raised.

tokens.name: ink-tertiary
tokens.usage: Lowest-emphasis text that is still text: placeholder, disabled label, gutter line numbers, breadcrumb separators. Holds 4.5:1 on surface-canvas, surface-base, surface-raised and surface-sunken in both themes.

tokens.name: ink-inverse
tokens.usage: Text and icons on a filled ink-primary ground, such as a keyboard-shortcut badge in the command palette.

tokens.name: accent
tokens.usage: Interactive intent and nothing else: links, primary button fill, active nav item, selection edge, focus. Never used to mean a run state. On surface-base and surface-raised.

tokens.name: accent-hover
tokens.usage: Hover and press for anything painted with accent.

tokens.name: accent-subtle
tokens.usage: Ground of the active sidebar item and of an accent-toned inline hint. Carries ink-primary or accent.

tokens.name: on-accent
tokens.usage: Text and icons on an accent fill. Light theme puts near-white on deep teal; dark theme puts near-black on bright teal — do not hardcode white.

tokens.name: status-running
tokens.usage: The running state: label text, chip text, icon, the left rail of a running row, an active graph edge in a run overlay. On surface-base and on status-running-bg.

tokens.name: status-running-bg
tokens.usage: Chip and rail tint behind status-running text.

tokens.name: status-waiting
tokens.usage: Waiting on a human — a gate or a permission ask. The loudest status in the system and the only one allowed in the title bar and sidebar counts. On surface-base and on status-waiting-bg.

tokens.name: status-waiting-bg
tokens.usage: Chip, rail and attention-inbox row tint behind status-waiting text.

tokens.name: status-succeeded
tokens.usage: Succeeded and completed. Used at chip scale only — success is the expected outcome and never fills a row. On surface-base and on status-succeeded-bg.

tokens.name: status-succeeded-bg
tokens.usage: Chip tint behind status-succeeded text.

tokens.name: status-failed
tokens.usage: Failed steps, failed runs, failed dependencies, handshake errors. On surface-base and on status-failed-bg.

tokens.name: status-failed-bg
tokens.usage: Chip and rail tint behind status-failed text.

tokens.name: status-cancelled
tokens.usage: Cancelled by a person. Neutral by design: a cancel is not a fault. Always drawn with the slashed-circle glyph. On surface-base and on status-cancelled-bg.

tokens.name: status-cancelled-bg
tokens.usage: Chip tint behind status-cancelled text.

tokens.name: status-blocked
tokens.usage: Blocked by an open dependency. Distinct from failed because nothing went wrong and from waiting because no person is being asked. On surface-base and on status-blocked-bg.

tokens.name: status-blocked-bg
tokens.usage: Chip tint behind status-blocked text.

tokens.name: status-held
tokens.usage: Held by the scheduler: ready to run but restrained by risk exposure or appetite. On surface-base and on status-held-bg.

tokens.name: status-held-bg
tokens.usage: Chip tint behind status-held text.

tokens.name: status-stale
tokens.usage: Data older than the live connection: last-known values while reconnecting or disconnected. Neutral like cancelled — tell them apart by the clock glyph and the dashed border, never by hue. On surface-base and on status-stale-bg.

tokens.name: status-stale-bg
tokens.usage: Chip tint behind status-stale text, and the ground of a stale-data banner.

tokens.name: diff-add-bg
tokens.usage: Added lines in an artifact version diff. Paired with a leading plus sign, never colour alone.

tokens.name: diff-remove-bg
tokens.usage: Removed lines in an artifact version diff. Paired with a leading minus sign.

tokens.name: graph-edge
tokens.usage: Workflow and dependency graph edges that a run did not traverse, and the run-tree indent guides. Holds 3:1 on surface-canvas, surface-base and surface-raised — graph structure is meaningful non-text content, so it is never drawn at hairline strength.

tokens.name: graph-edge-active
tokens.usage: Edges on the path a run actually took, and a satisfied dependency edge. Carries an arrowhead as well as the colour.

tokens.name: risk-low
tokens.usage: Risk matrix cell ground, exposure band 1–4. Carries ink-primary.

tokens.name: risk-moderate
tokens.usage: Risk matrix cell ground, exposure band 5–9. Carries ink-primary.

tokens.name: risk-high
tokens.usage: Risk matrix cell ground, exposure band 10–14. Carries ink-primary.

tokens.name: risk-severe
tokens.usage: Risk matrix cell ground, exposure band 15–25, above the default appetite line. Carries ink-primary and a hatched overlay so the band survives greyscale.

type.note: Two tracks. Sans carries the interface; mono carries everything ORCA produced — ids, step names, node names, paths, agent output, artifact bodies. A reader should be able to tell at a glance whether a string came from a person or from the system.

families.sans: "IBM Plex Sans", "Segoe UI", Ubuntu, Cantarell, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
families.mono: "IBM Plex Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, "DejaVu Sans Mono", monospace

styles.name: display
styles.usage: The one large heading on an empty state or a first-run screen. Not used in the shell.

styles.name: title
styles.usage: Screen title in the object header: a request summary, a plan name, a config file name.

styles.name: heading
styles.usage: Pane headers, section headers in a config form, card titles.

styles.name: body
styles.usage: Default interface text: row labels, prose, field values, menu items.

styles.name: body-strong
styles.usage: The one emphasised thing in a row — a work item title, a gate question, the agent name in a tool call.

styles.name: label
styles.usage: Secondary row text, table cells, timestamps, form labels, button text.

styles.name: label-strong
styles.usage: Column headers, chip text, active tab, the label of a focused field.

styles.name: caption
styles.usage: Field help, counts, relative times, the second line of a two-line row.

styles.name: eyebrow
styles.usage: Uppercase group headers in the sidebar and the command palette. Sentence content is never set in this style.

styles.name: mono-body
styles.usage: Artifact bodies, YAML source, step and node names, file paths, expressions.

styles.name: mono-strong
styles.usage: The name of the thing itself in a row: a workflow node name, a tool name, a changed key in a diff.

styles.name: mono-log
styles.usage: Streamed agent output and tool-call payloads. Line height is tight enough that a screen of log is worth scrolling and loose enough to read.

styles.name: mono-id
styles.usage: Run ids, event ids, commit shas, artifact versions. Tracked out slightly so a truncated id can still be compared by eye.

spacing.note: A 4px grid. Everything in the shell lands on it; the only sub-grid value is space-0-5 for hairline-adjacent gaps.

tokens.name: space-0-5
tokens.usage: Gap between a status glyph and its label; chip inner leading.

tokens.name: space-1
tokens.usage: Tightest gap: icon to text, chip to chip.

tokens.name: space-2
tokens.usage: Inline gap inside a row, cell padding in a compact table, gap between chips.

tokens.name: space-3
tokens.usage: Row horizontal padding, gap between a label and its control, one run-tree indent step.

tokens.name: space-4
tokens.usage: Pane padding, card padding, gap between form fields.

tokens.name: space-5
tokens.usage: Gap between a card's header and its body.

tokens.name: space-6
tokens.usage: Gap between sections within a pane; command palette padding.

tokens.name: space-8
tokens.usage: Gap between major blocks on a screen; empty-state inset.

tokens.name: space-12
tokens.usage: Top and bottom inset of a centred empty or error state.

tokens.name: space-16
tokens.usage: The largest inset, used once per screen at most.

radius.note: Tight. A paper-and-ink system reads as drawn, not moulded; nothing in the shell is rounder than 10px and nothing is a pill except a status dot.

tokens.name: radius-none
tokens.usage: Table cells, pane edges, the risk matrix, full-bleed rows.

tokens.name: radius-xs
tokens.usage: Chips, badges, keyboard-shortcut keys, inline code.

tokens.name: radius-sm
tokens.usage: Buttons, inputs, selects, tree rows when selected.

tokens.name: radius-md
tokens.usage: Cards, graph nodes, the expanded step frame, tool-call rows.

tokens.name: radius-lg
tokens.usage: Floating surfaces: command palette, dialogs, popovers.

tokens.name: radius-full
tokens.usage: Status dots and the run progress meter cap only.

shadow.note: Elevation is scarce. Structure comes from hairlines; shadow means only 'this floats above the window' and appears on at most one element at a time.

tokens.name: shadow-none
tokens.usage: The default for every pane, card, row and graph node.

tokens.name: shadow-popover
tokens.usage: Menus, popovers, the schedule explanation bubble, autocomplete.

tokens.name: shadow-modal
tokens.usage: Command palette and dialogs, over surface-overlay.

tokens.name: shadow-sticky
tokens.usage: A sticky header that currently has content scrolled beneath it — applied only while scrolled, so the seam appears when it means something.

size.note: Two row heights carry the whole app. Comfortable is the default; compact is the density toggle, persisted per surface.

tokens.name: row-comfortable
tokens.usage: Default height of a run tree row, timeline entry, table row, list item.

tokens.name: row-compact
tokens.usage: The same rows under the density toggle, for trees of hundreds of steps.

tokens.name: control-sm
tokens.usage: Icon buttons, chips with an action, inline selects in a table.

tokens.name: control-md
tokens.usage: Default button, input, select.

tokens.name: control-lg
tokens.usage: Gate answer buttons and the command palette input — the controls that carry consequence.

tokens.name: icon-sm
tokens.usage: Status glyph inside a chip, disclosure triangle.

tokens.name: icon-md
tokens.usage: Row icons, node type glyphs, sidebar icons.

tokens.name: sidebar-width
tokens.usage: The primary sidebar. Collapsible to icon-only at 48px.

tokens.name: panel-width
tokens.usage: The docked right panel that holds artifacts. Resizable between 320px and 720px.

tokens.name: measure-prose
tokens.usage: Maximum line length for artifact prose and long-form guidance.

border.note: Widths only; the colours are the border-* and status-* colour tokens.

tokens.name: stroke-hairline
tokens.usage: Every separator and container edge in the system.

tokens.name: stroke-rail
tokens.usage: The left status rail on a run tree row or attention row, and the active-tab underline.

tokens.name: stroke-focus
tokens.usage: The focus ring, drawn with a 1px offset outside the control.

tokens.name: stroke-edge-active
tokens.usage: A workflow graph edge on the executed path; untraversed edges stay at stroke-hairline.

duration.note: Motion is used for orientation only — disclosure, panel entry, the running pulse. Nothing in this system animates to celebrate. All of it is suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion, where the running state falls back to the animated glyph being replaced by a static one.

tokens.name: duration-instant
tokens.usage: Hover and selection feedback: no transition, so a fast keyboard user never sees a lagging highlight.

tokens.name: duration-fast
tokens.usage: Disclosure open and close, chip state change, tab switch.

tokens.name: duration-medium
tokens.usage: Right panel and command palette entry and exit.

tokens.name: duration-pulse
tokens.usage: One cycle of the running-state pulse on a status dot and of the streaming caret.

easing.note: Two curves. Anything that enters uses ease-entrance; anything that changes in place uses ease-standard.

tokens.name: ease-standard
tokens.usage: In-place changes: disclosure, resize, tab underline.

tokens.name: ease-entrance
tokens.usage: Panels, palette and popovers arriving.

tokens.name: ease-linear
tokens.usage: The running pulse and the indeterminate progress track only.

opacity.note: Three uses, no more. Opacity never carries a status on its own.

tokens.name: opacity-disabled
tokens.usage: A disabled control. Always paired with aria-disabled and an unchanged label colour token beneath.

tokens.name: opacity-stale
tokens.usage: Last-known values while disconnected, applied to the value only and never to its label.

tokens.name: opacity-untaken
tokens.usage: Workflow graph nodes and edges a run did not traverse, in the run-overlay view.
